core_idea: Supervised: action = f(obs, language). Action chunking + flow/diffusion head on a VLM backbone.
representative_methods: ACT, Diffusion Policy, SmolVLA, pi0, GR00T, X-VLA, OpenVLA
strengths: Mature, stable, best tooling (LeRobot). Directly deployable.
limitations: Capped by demo quantity/quality; can't learn from failures; OOD-brittle.
haller_note: Your teleop data feeds this directly.

core_idea: Learn a predictive model of environment dynamics; plan or train policy inside 'imagined' rollouts.
representative_methods: Dreamer V3, DayDreamer, TD-MPC2, DreMa, Ctrl-World, World4RL
strengths: Sample-efficient; can imagine novel configs (DreMa: 1-shot); learn from imagined futures without real rollouts.
limitations: Hard to make physically accurate; hallucination; heavier to build.
haller_note: DreMa-style needs Gaussian-splat scene capture; strong data-amplification idea.

core_idea: Extract latent actions from action-less video (VQ-VAE / IDM), pretrain, then map latent->robot with few demos.
representative_methods: LAPA, UniVLA, Moto, GR-2, Being-H0, DreamGen, EMMA (mobile)
strengths: Breaks the data bottleneck: internet-scale + your own phone videos; strong for generalization & new tasks.
limitations: Latent actions noisy; embodiment gap; needs a mapping-finetune step on real robot.
haller_note: You can record human videos of the task cheaply; EMMA (arXiv:2509.04443, ref not read directly - verify) targets MOBILE manip specifically.

core_idea: Start from a BC/VLA policy, improve online or offline with rewards; learn from the robot's own failures.
representative_methods: SimpleVLA-RL, VLA-RL, ConRFT, ReWiND, pi_RL, RLDG
strengths: Beats pure imitation OOD; ReWiND reports ~5x improvement in ~1h online (author-reported); self-improves in deployment.
limitations: Reward design hard in real world; resets/safety; sample cost on real hardware.
haller_note: The path to 'better than your demos'. Pairs with world models to cut real rollouts.

core_idea: One model co-trained on real robot + human video + sim/neural-generated video via shared latent action space.
strengths: The closest thing to 'humanoid-level generalist'; combines all paradigms above; cross-embodiment.
limitations: Huge compute to pretrain (GR00T: ~50k H100-hrs, author-reported); you FINE-TUNE, not pretrain.
haller_note: Fine-tune the open checkpoint on your data; conceptually unifies everything.

core_idea: Self-supervised joint-embedding world model predicts in LATENT space; act by PLANNING (MPC/CEM) toward a goal-image latent, not by learning a reactive policy.
strengths: No action labels needed; learns from passive internet video + tiny robot data; zero-shot to new arms/labs/objects; goal-image conditioned; open weights (V-JEPA 2).
limitations: Planning is slow (~16s/action, author-reported) vs reactive VLAs; goal-IMAGE not language; not a drop-in LeRobot policy; needs an MPC/controller wrapper.
haller_note: V-JEPA 2 open + works from a monocular cam zero-shot; strong for LEARNING the world-model-planning paradigm. Goal-image fits fixed setups; slower loop is fine for study, not fast tasks.
